examples.input: Julius Caesar drafted an email to his generals before crossing the Rubicon.
Julius Caesar sent written dispatches to his generals before crossing the Rubicon.
Benjamin Franklin tweeted a witty remark about electricity after his kite experiment.
Benjamin Franklin penned a witty remark about electricity in a letter after his kite experiment.
Cleopatra held a video conference on Zoom with Roman envoys from her Alexandria palace.
Cleopatra met face to face with Roman envoys in her Alexandria palace.
Genghis Khan checked Google Maps on his smartphone to chart the fastest route across the Steppe.
Genghis Khan relied on experienced scouts to chart the fastest route across the Steppe.
Mozart uploaded his new symphony to Spotify so patrons across Europe could hear it instantly.
Mozart premiered his new symphony in a Viennese concert hall so patrons across Europe could hear it.
Leonardo da Vinci posted a time-lapse of The Last Supper on Instagram Stories.
Leonardo da Vinci sketched studies of The Last Supper in his notebooks.
George Washington sent a mass text message to Continental Army officers about the surprise attack on Trenton.
George Washington sent mounted couriers to Continental Army officers about the surprise attack on Trenton.
Joan of Arc coordinated her units using military-grade walkie-talkies during the Siege of Orleans.
Joan of Arc coordinated her units by relaying messages through flag bearers during the Siege of Orleans.
Queen Victoria watched a live BBC television broadcast of the Diamond Jubilee procession.
Queen Victoria watched the Diamond Jubilee procession from a carriage window.
Ernest Hemingway opened his laptop and connected to cafe Wi-Fi to revise A Moveable Feast in 1920s Paris.
Ernest Hemingway sat with a portable typewriter to revise A Moveable Feast in 1920s Paris.
